nn_reference.kind: first bar meeting all flush conditions (suppressed by the 7-day decluster)

current.nn_note: descriptive; reference episode chosen after the fact; features z-scored over historical events before 2026-11-08

rule_candidates.rule: WHEN a crypto perp has just printed a flush (48h return below its 1y 5th pct, OI down >= 5% from its 72h high, v0 R9) THEN do not buy the next 4h close expecting a rebound: the low usually comes later
rule_candidates.when: flush event: 4h close with 48h log return below its trailing-1y 5th pct, 4h OI >= 5% below its 72h high, v0 cell R9 (post_cascade_study.flush_events); candidate is a long entered within the first 4h after the event
rule_candidates.then: expect a negative net R for a rebound long at the next 4h close with a stop under the flush low (2R target, 5-day time stop), and worse than a random long in the same R9 cell
rule_candidates.effect: net R per trade, 7.5 bp/side: llm_in_sample -0.19 [-0.36, -0.00] (n 614, 116 weeks), clean_holdout -0.34 [-0.67, -0.15] (n 22, 8 weeks); minus matched R9 random longs -0.35 [-0.59, -0.12] / -0.25 [-0.67, +0.08]; pegged-limit entry changes it by < 0.01 R
rule_candidates.review: a registered later-entry variant (e.g. after the R9 episode ends or after a confirmed higher low) tested the same way; 20+ more holdout events

rule_candidates.rule: WHEN a flush has just printed THEN expect the 7-day low still ahead (median a further 5-9% down, usually one to three days later and later still in the 2026 holdout) followed by a rebound of about 8-15% off that low, with no net drift over the week
rule_candidates.when: flush event: 4h close with 48h log return below its trailing-1y 5th pct, 4h OI >= 5% below its 72h high, v0 cell R9 (post_cascade_study.flush_events)
rule_candidates.then: describes the path from the event close over 7 days (1h bars); use it to set expectations for timing, not as a direction signal
rule_candidates.effect: pooled n 636: further drop to the 7-day low median -8.7% (IQR -15.8% to -4.2%), low after median 54 h (only 35% within 24 h), rebound from the low median +15.1%, 7-day return median +0.3%; BTC n 41: -5.4%, 36 h, +12.8%; clean_holdout n 22: -6.8%, 127 h, +8.0%
rule_candidates.review: descriptive, mostly in-sample; re-check the holdout path quantiles at 50+ holdout events

rule_candidates.rule: WHEN the R9 episode that contains a flush ends THEN expect R6 whipsaw next (about 80%), otherwise R8 trend down; R9 itself usually lasts another 1-2.5 days after the flush
rule_candidates.when: flush event: 4h close with 48h log return below its trailing-1y 5th pct, 4h OI >= 5% below its 72h high, v0 cell R9 (post_cascade_study.flush_events); v0 cell on 4h bars (regimes.label, bar_hours 4)
rule_candidates.then: describes the state path; refines R-PX-8 (62% whipsaw after R9 in general) for flush-led R9 episodes
rule_candidates.effect: first cell after R9: R6 80%, R8 18% (n 635; BTC R6 83%, clean_holdout R6 81% of 21); R9 hours left after the event median 36 (IQR 20-60); cell at +7d: R6 30%, R9 25%, R5 18%, R8 13%
rule_candidates.review: the same matrix on daily cells, or a holdout share of R6 below 60% at 40+ holdout events

rule_candidates.rule: WHEN funding drops below its 90-day 10th percentile while open interest rebuilds >= 3% within 72h of a flush THEN don't expect a short squeeze from it: the next 24h is if anything weaker than after flushes without that pattern
rule_candidates.when: flush event: 4h close with 48h log return below its trailing-1y 5th pct, 4h OI >= 5% below its 72h high, v0 cell R9 (post_cascade_study.flush_events); then at a 4h close within 72h: latest funding print < trailing-90d 10th pct of prints and OI >= 3% above its post-flush low
rule_candidates.then: treat new shorts piling in after a flush as no evidence for a rebound (in line with R-AVOID-1 / R-MAP-5 on funding-contrarian signals)
rule_candidates.effect: pattern minus no-pattern vol-scaled return, llm_in_sample 24h -0.14 [-0.32, +0.02] sigma, 72h +0.02 [-0.13, +0.17] (pattern 234 of 614 events); clean_holdout 24h -0.39 [-1.13, +0.66], 72h +0.02 [-0.61, +0.74] (pattern 4 of 35)

rule_candidates.rule: WHEN shorting the first 4h close back below the EMA20 after a >= 1.5 sigma post-flush rebound THEN expect about breakeven net R: better than a random short in the same cell, but no edge yet
rule_candidates.when: flush event: 4h close with 48h log return below its trailing-1y 5th pct, 4h OI >= 5% below its 72h high, v0 cell R9 (post_cascade_study.flush_events); then within 7 days a close >= 1.5 sigma above the post-flush low, then a 4h close crossing below the 4h EMA20
rule_candidates.then: a short here is not worse than other shorts in the whipsaw that follows, but there is no tested positive expectation
rule_candidates.effect: net R per trade: llm_in_sample -0.00 [-0.15, +0.15] (n 560), clean_holdout +0.42 [-0.42, +1.21] (n 19, 7 weeks); minus matched random shorts +0.15 [-0.01, +0.32] / +0.65 [-0.41, +1.56]; entries mostly in R6 (351 of 560)
rule_candidates.review: holdout CI clearing zero at 40+ trades, or a registered variant
